root_idea.summary: A semantic orientation toward restless movement, circling, and evasive maneuvering.
root_idea.development: The root lexicon connects the fish with continual motion and extends the image of its movement to circling around something and maneuvering or beguiling another person.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The single Quran-attested nominal group is published under the normalized singular citation form.

senses.definition: A fish, including a large or great fish; in the Jonah narrative, the fish that swallowed him.
senses.usage_conditions: Occurs in singular حوت and plural حيتان. In صاحب الحوت, “the companion of the fish,” the phrase is an epithet for Jonah.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go or circle around a thing; of a bird, to circle around water, and of a wild animal, to circle around.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with عَلَى الشَّيْءِ or بِهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strive to turn or entice someone away from something; to maneuver or beguile him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be a person’s family, property, or another concern; the usage is figurative, likened to the movement of a fish in water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strive or contend with someone in order to repel him.
To consult someone or confer with him.
To negotiate with someone through consultation or promises in a sale.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional commercial usage of the derived Form III verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The constellation Pisces; by extension, the Southern Fish and the bright star Fomalhaut described as being in its mouth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An astronomical usage marked as figurative or extended.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fish-like, fish-related, or resembling a great fish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may be used figuratively of someone who swallows like a fish.
The entry itself directs the fuller treatment of this word to حَيٌّ.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Circling or going around is represented under حَاتَ.
Turning, enticing, and beguiling are represented under حَاوَتَ.
Contending to repel is represented separately.
Consulting or conferring is represented separately.
Consulting or making promises in a sale is represented as a commercial usage.
The fish meaning is represented by the Quran-attested noun sense.
The Quranic epithet صاحب الحوت is covered in the sense conditions.
The astronomical meaning is represented under حُوتٌ.
The fish-related adjective and figurative swallowing usage are represented.
The serpent-male meaning is represented under حَيُّوتٌ.

cautions: The lexical description includes “great fish,” while the supplied Quran contextual glosses uniformly say “fish”; the size qualification should not be imposed on every Quranic occurrence.
